title: Transparency: The Unspoken Design Element -- How Levels of Visibility Affect Adult Learning and Sharing
research_question:
1. How are space and materials used to create and disseminate visibility?
2. How does visibility relate to the social/ psychological aspects of privacy, trust, and the overall culture within a space?
3. How do the differing levels of transparency ultimately affect learning and sharing?

participants.description: High school students, university students, and workplace employees in San Diego County, California, and Little Rock, Arkansas.
participants.recruitment: Interviews with users were chosen over general surveys to ask probing questions and get a deeper sense of the meaning behind feedback.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: High Tech High (HTH) facilities (Gary and Jerri-Ann Jacobs HTH, HTH International Building, HTH Chula Vista) in San Diego County, California.
University of Arkansas-Little Rock (UALR) facilities (George W. Donaghey College of Engineering and Information Technology building, College of Business building) in Little Rock, Arkansas.
Heifer International headquarters facility in Little Rock, Arkansas.

measures.construct: User activity and behavior in learning and working environments
Perceptions of privacy, social status, territory, control, creativity, and productivity

findings.antecedent: Highly visible design (open plan, glass partitions, eroded corners, translucent materials) at high school facility
findings.consequent: Active and informal environment
findings.quote: At the high school facility, the highly visible design provided an active and informal environment.

findings.antecedent: Highly visible design (open plan, glass partitions, eroded corners, translucent materials) at high school facility
findings.consequent: Student collaboration and use of corridors/open areas for meetings
findings.quote: Students worked in collaboration with one another and used the corridors and open areas to meet.

findings.antecedent: Spaces adjacent to classrooms with high visibility at high school facility
findings.consequent: Teachers' passive supervision of students dispersed in groups
findings.quote: Teachers made use of the spaces adjacent to their classroom in order to supervise students that were dispersed in groups.

findings.antecedent: Open environment with high visibility at high school facility
findings.consequent: Student distraction and disengagement from focused work to interact socially
findings.quote: Intermittently, students appeared to become distracted and disengage from focused work to interact with peers on a social level.

findings.antecedent: Nature of the curriculum (project-based learning) and design of the high school facility (high visibility)
findings.consequent: Social connectivity seamlessly woven into learning methods and practices
findings.quote: Due to the nature of the curriculum and design of the facility, social connectivity appeared to weave seamlessly into learning methods and practices.

findings.antecedent: Light-filled café and open break areas at university facility
findings.consequent: Student gravitation towards these areas for group work and informal gatherings
findings.quote: Students gravitated toward the light-filled café downstairs and its counterpart, the open break area, upstairs.

findings.antecedent: Open areas with blurred boundaries at university facility
findings.consequent: Students creating temporary social boundaries or delineations when not collaborating
findings.quote: In these open areas with blurred boundaries, students appeared to create temporary social boundaries or delineations.

findings.antecedent: Open plan and transparent material usage at workplace facility
findings.consequent: Formation of user habits in semi-private and public areas (e.g., using headphones for privacy)
findings.quote: The workplace observation periods demonstrated how user habits form in semi-private and public areas of the facility.

findings.antecedent: Open plan and transparent material usage at workplace facility
findings.consequent: Employees opening themselves up for social interaction or higher volume conversations in break areas
findings.quote: employees that enter the break area appear to be opening themselves up for social interaction or higher volume conversations.

findings.antecedent: Open plan environment at the workstation (low partitions) at workplace facility
findings.consequent: Ease of information transmission (quick conversations over partitions)
findings.quote: The open plan environment at the workstation seems to lend to productivity in terms of ease of information transmission.

findings.antecedent: Environmental settings (open, visible, flexible) at high school facility
findings.consequent: Setting the stage for student expectations and directing students towards certain studying/collaborating styles
findings.quote: The environmental settings appear to set the stage for student expectations and teachers are often the directors which lead the students toward a certain style or type of studying and collaborating.

findings.antecedent: Students' emphasis on behavioral control and freedom to modify their environment at high school facility
findings.consequent: Increased satisfaction and confidence
findings.quote: The students placed an emphasis on the amount of behavioral control they have and the freedom to modify their environment.

findings.antecedent: Open environment with high visibility at high school facility
findings.consequent: Students' ability to function well due to not feeling judged and having freedom to express themselves
findings.quote: Social components of the behavior-setting theory show that the students are able to function well in an open environment because they do not feel judged and have freedom to express themselves.

findings.antecedent: Open environment with high visibility at high school facility
findings.consequent: Student preference for acoustical privacy over visual privacy when working or learning
findings.quote: Also, they prefer acoustical privacy over visual privacy when working or learning.

findings.antecedent: Variety of different spaces and flexibility at high school facility
findings.consequent: Accommodation of different student work styles and provision of added perception of control
findings.quote: Lastly, a variety of different spaces to work in and flexibility was a key component to accommodating different student work styles and providing students with the added perception of control.

findings.antecedent: Lack of territory and general sense of ownership to the university learning environment (due to transient use)
findings.consequent: Lower initial sense of belonging among students
findings.quote: Students within the university facility suggest a lack of territory and general sense of ownership to their learning environment.

findings.antecedent: Familiarity with being a college student and/or the campus itself
findings.consequent: Greater sense of belonging among university students
findings.quote: The results suggest that students, once they have become familiar with the idea of being a college student and/or perhaps the campus itself, feel a greater sense of belonging when they are attending class.

findings.antecedent: Student's personality and availability of informal areas vs. home/quiet library for study
findings.consequent: Choice in where to collaborate or seek connection
findings.quote: Answers suggest that depending on the student’s personality, he or she will position himself or prefer to study on campus in more informal areas, or the opposite- at his home or in the quiet nature of the library.

findings.antecedent: Visual privacy (less of an issue) at university facility
findings.consequent: Acoustical privacy and noise control being more of an issue than visual access to others
findings.quote: Regarding visual privacy, the students all found acoustical privacy and noise control to be more of an issue than visual access to others.

findings.antecedent: Personal detachment or lack of territory at university facility (due to temporary use)
findings.consequent: Unwillingness to modify the general setup or make long-term changes to furniture/structures
findings.quote: A personal detachment or lack of territory led them to believe that because others would need the space, they should not modify the general set up or make any long-term changes.

findings.antecedent: Affordance of permanence and territory within the workplace environment (long-term employees, personal workstation)
findings.consequent: Enhanced sense of belonging and territory among employees
findings.quote: The answers from the interviewees at the workplace facility support the notion that the employees are afforded a sense of permanence and territory within the environment.

findings.antecedent: Variety of workspace options at workplace facility (depending on type of work)
findings.consequent: Increased ability to focus and work individually
findings.quote: Also, employees suggest that they have a variety of workspace options in which to use depending on the type of work at hand.

findings.antecedent: Feedback and communication primarily happening digitally outside of separate meetings at workplace facility
findings.consequent: Reduced need for in-person interruptions
findings.quote: Feedback and communication happens primarily digitally outside of separate meetings.

findings.antecedent: Employees' ability to make decisions on how they work individually and what aids their focus at workplace facility
findings.consequent: Increased ability to focus
findings.quote: Regarding control, employees can make decisions on how they work individually and what can aid in their ability to focus.

findings.antecedent: Rarely an issue with visual visibility at workplace facility
findings.consequent: Acoustical privacy becoming a constraint if lacking
findings.quote: The employees also stated that they rarely have an issue with visibility but acoustical privacy can become a constraint if it is lacking.

findings.antecedent: Permanent, all-day program of the workplace facility and established behavioral/social norms
findings.consequent: Increased respect for others’ time and space
findings.quote: Because of the permanent, all-day program of the workplace facility, behavioral and social norms have come into play in order to respect others’ time and space.

findings.antecedent: Culture of the organization promoting high levels of equality and openness of the design at workplace facility
findings.consequent: Manifestation of equality
findings.quote: Along with this, the culture of the organization promotes high levels of equality which are manifested in the openness of the design.

findings.antecedent: High levels of visibility within learning and working environments
findings.consequent: Increased passive supervision
findings.mechanism: ability to facilitate a group without being directly and physically next to the others at all times.
findings.quote: Passive supervision is the ability to facilitate a group without being directly and physically next to the others at all times.

findings.antecedent: Transparent materials used to create segmented and contained spaces
findings.consequent: Feeling of not being closed off while providing privacy (particularly through acoustics)
findings.quote: Transparent materials can be used to create segmented and contained spaces that do not feel closed off yet they can still provide privacy, particularly through acoustics, as needed.

findings.antecedent: Not being directly supervised (due to passive supervision)
findings.consequent: Increased freedom and trust
findings.quote: When one is not directly supervised, an increase in freedom and trust begins to surface.

findings.antecedent: Spaces planned with visibility in mind
findings.consequent: Increased feeling of control over one’s environment
findings.quote: When spaces are planned with visibility in mind, an increased feeling of control over one’s environment can be seen.

findings.antecedent: Visual privacy (less important than acoustic privacy)
findings.consequent: Acoustical privacy and noise control being more of an issue than visual access to others
findings.quote: In this study, visual privacy was less important than being able to limit what others could hear.

findings.antecedent: User's ability to manipulate his or her environment for added flexibility
findings.consequent: Increased ability to meet productivity needs
findings.quote: Similarly, territory is important because the user can manipulate his or her environment for added flexibility to meet productivity needs.

findings.antecedent: Highly visible atmospheres (e.g., eroded corners, lower workstations)
findings.consequent: Increased awareness and control over the happenings in and around one's environment
findings.quote: The former scenario provides the inhabitant with much more awareness and control over the happenings in and around his environment.

findings.antecedent: Informal environment (high visibility, natural light, less formalities)
findings.consequent: Increased communication and less formalities in general
findings.quote: An informal environment contributes to more communication and less formalities in general.

findings.antecedent: Cafes, break out areas, widened corridors, and other opportunities for conversation (nodes)
findings.consequent: Contribution to an informal environment
findings.quote: Cafes, break out areas, widened corridors, and other opportunities for conversation (in the preference framework, known as “nodes”), can be utilized to add to an informal environment.

findings.antecedent: Opportunities for conversation and social interaction
findings.consequent: Creation of heightened trust among peers, leading to greater sense of belonging
findings.quote: Also, as social beings, these opportunities create heightened trust among peers which leads to greater sense of belonging.

findings.antecedent: High levels of visibility within learning or working environments
findings.consequent: Allowing users to participate vicariously in others’ projects
findings.quote: High levels of visibility within learning or working environments allow users to participate vicariously in other’s projects.

findings.antecedent: Vicarious participation in others’ projects (fosters elevated work)
findings.consequent: Healthy competition or a reminder of the goal at hand
findings.quote: Naturally, this fosters elevated work among a group because healthy competition can arise or even just a reminder of the goal at hand.

findings.antecedent: Use of transparency leading to openness (seeing what others are working on)
findings.consequent: Increased collaboration and creativity
findings.quote: Collaboration and creativity could be increased due to inquiry about a project and thoughts exchanged where they might not have if work was never shared.

findings.antecedent: Incorporating the element of transparency into a design
findings.consequent: Increased display of culture
findings.quote: An increased display of culture is the last result of incorporating the element of transparency into a design.

findings.antecedent: Literal transparency (revealing inner workings of an organization)
findings.consequent: Increased understanding of the overall mission
findings.quote: Literal transparency has a way of acting phenomenally in terms of revealing what an organization is all about.

findings.antecedent: Transparent environment that displays a deeper motive
findings.consequent: Enhancement of the mysterious aspect of Kaplan’s preference framework
findings.quote: Additionally, a transparent environment that displays a deeper motive could be said to enhance the mysterious aspect of Kaplan’s preference framework.

findings.antecedent: Active, purpose-driven environment which tells a story
findings.consequent: Provision of stimulation (as opposed to a predictable, monotonous feel)
findings.quote: An active, purpose-driven environment which tells a story is thought to provide stimulation, as opposed to a predictable, monotonous feel.

mechanisms: Passive supervision (ability to facilitate a group without being directly and physically next to the others at all times)
Increased feeling of control over one's environment (due to awareness of surroundings and ability to manipulate space)
Informal environment (leading to more communication and less formalities)
Fosters elevated work (through vicarious participation, healthy competition, and reminders of goals)
Increased display of culture (revealing organizational mission and enhancing mystery)
moderators: Nature of the curriculum and design of the facility
implementation_implications: Designers should consider transparency to meld organizational goals with design outcomes.
Transparent physical attributes of an interior space can manifest a feeling of social and psychological openness.
Designing with transparency can propel openness towards success for learning and working environments.
Prioritize acoustical privacy over visual privacy in open, transparent designs.
Provide a variety of spaces and flexibility to accommodate different work styles and increase perceived control.
In university settings, consider project-based innovation centers to foster ownership and territory.
limitations: The variety of work a student, college student, or employee might be doing (e.g., not including creative fields like architecture or graphic design).
The lessened sense of ownership and territory in university settings due to temporary user status.
The influence of teacher’s and managerial presence on an institution, acknowledging the complexity of architectural determinism.

mechanism_chain.description: Increased visibility in design reduces perceived barriers, fostering greater awareness and opportunities for spontaneous interaction, which leads to a more active and informal environment conducive to learning and sharing.

steps.from_construct: highly visible design elements (e.g., glass partitions, open plan)
steps.to_construct: increased visual access and awareness of others' activities
reduced perceived social barriers and increased opportunities for spontaneous interaction

steps.from_construct: reduced perceived social barriers and increased opportunities for interaction
steps.to_construct: more frequent and informal social interactions and collaborations
